title: Guarding One’s Gaze in Islam
summary: The importance of controlling one's gaze as per Islamic teachings to avoid sin. Lowering the gaze is linked to purity, as instructed in the Quran, and lewd gazing is considered the 'Mother of Evils.' It is described as a poisoned arrow and is harmful, leading to inner moral corruption. A sudden glance may be forgivable, but intentional looks with lust break character and diminish spiritual delight. Muslims are advised to avoid it to maintain the sweetness of faith and worship.
translation: Looking at inappropriate things is a grave sin. The Quran specifically instructs believing men and women to restrain their gaze and protect their chastity. The verse says, "Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their private parts; that is purer for them. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what they do." When a person's eyes become uncontrolled, it often leads to immorality and is the root of many evils. Scholars call lewd gazing the 'Mother of Evils.' In the teachings of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), it is said that the gaze is a poisoned arrow of Iblis (Satan). A glance injects poison into the heart. The 'zina of the eyes' is to look with lust. If a person gazes at a non-mahram with lust, it is as though committing adultery in the heart. However, a sudden glance is forgivable, but intentionally and repeatedly looking with lust at a non-mahram causes significant harm and robs one of the delight of good deeds, as Satan embellishes the faces of non-mahrams. Even from a distance, everything may appear attractive. Consequently, once a seed of sin is planted in the heart, one tends to seek sinful opportunities. Imam Ghazali (may Allah have mercy on him) said a glance creates a thought, which turns into desire and leads to intention. If a Muslim sees a woman's beauty once and then lowers their gaze, Allah rewards them with the delight of worship. Another hadith states that anyone who refrains from lewd gazing for fear of Allah will receive faith that they will feel the sweetness of in their heart. This sin is prevalent, so everyone, regardless of age or gender, should strive to avoid it. It is a dangerous sin, which sometimes deprives a person of the sweetness of worship.
